title: Two Uniswap v4 instances list Token Addresses that belong to the corresponding Curve pools
content:
The Uniswap v4 PYUSD/USDS instance records Token Address `0xa632d59b9b804a956bfaa9b48af3a1b74808fc1f` (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.11.1.2.2.1). The Curve pyUSD/USDS Pool instance records Token Address `0xA632D59b9B804a956BfaA9b48Af3A1b74808FC1f` (.7.4.2.2.1) — the same address, differing only in checksum casing. The Uniswap v4 USDT/USDS instance records `0x00836Fe54625BE242BcFA286207795405ca4fD10` (.11.2.2.2.1), which the Curve sUSDS/USDT instance also records as its Token Address (.7.1.2.2.1).

Both cannot be right. A Curve pool's LP token is a deployed ERC-20 belonging to that pool; a Uniswap v4 pool has no LP token at all, which is precisely why the other two v4 instances list only a Pool ID. The v4 entries also reuse the pair labels `PYUSDUSDS` and `USDTUSDS`, and the Curve instances use `PYUSDUSDS` and `sUSDSUSDT`.

The most economical explanation is that the v4 documents were created by copying the nearest equivalent Curve instance and updating the parameters that obviously differ — target protocol, ticks, fee — while carrying the address and token label across.

This matters beyond tidiness because addresses are the part of the Artifact that is mechanically checkable, and these are the entries a verifier would use to confirm which contract Spark is authorised to touch. It is also the second copy-paste fossil in this Artifact, after the Morpho placeholder names embedded in the Fluid ERC-4626 runbook: the template-cloning workflow that keeps the schema uniform is itself the source of these defects.
description: The v4 PYUSD/USDS and USDT/USDS instances repeat 0xa632d59b… and 0x00836Fe5… — the exact addresses recorded as Curve pool tokens elsewhere in the same Artifact, which cannot both be correct.
